
=================================================================
#58 Sulmun  (태초)  [FLASHBACK EPISODE]
Arc: The Fall of Euija · place: halla · tone: island folklore
Logline: Before the island there is a woman, and she is enormous.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ The next story is told to him on a roof, because he is on a roof, mending it, and Yuri Dora has decided that a man who will not sit down can still listen.
[1] Yuri Dora: Guests don’t mend roofs.
[2] Gyebek: I eat your rice. I mend your roof. / Then I owe nothing.
[3] Yuri Dora: And when the roof’s done?
[4] Gyebek: The wall.
[5] ¶ He drives a peg and counts it. Then, without looking down, he asks what he has wanted to ask all day.
[6] Gyebek: How far is the mainland.
[7] Yuri Dora: Two days, with a good wind. / Nobody here has a good wind for you, Turtle.
[8] Gyebek: Is there a bridge.
[9] Yuri Dora: Ha! There nearly was.
[10] Yuri Dora: One woman made this island. Sulmun.
[11] ¶ Before the island there is a woman, and she is enormous. **Sulmun**, the Great Lady. The sea comes to her knee. She scoops the seabed up in her apron and piles it in one place until it stands high enough to lean on, and that is **Mount Halla**.
[12] ¶ Some fell out on the way. The island counts three hundred and sixty-eight hills.
[13] [CARD Sulmun: Grandmother Sulmun. The sea comes to her knee, and she has opinions about the view.]
[14] [PLACE halla: The island’s spine, and a giantess’s favourite chair.]
[15] Gyebek: Was there a hole in the apron.
[16] Yuri Dora: …How did you know that?
[17] Gyebek: You said there are three hundred and sixty-eight hills. / If it were poured in one place there would be one.
[18] ¶ Yuri Dora looks at him for a while.
[19] Yuri Dora: You do not listen to a story. You inspect it.
[20] Gyebek: …Yes.
[21] ¶ She had five hundred sons. In a famine she set a cauldron of porridge to boil for them, and slipped, and did not come out. The sons ate. It was the best they had ever tasted, and they said so, and then the youngest reached the bottom and found his mother’s bones.
[22] ¶ The hammering stops.
[23] Gyebek: …They said it was good.
[24] Yuri Dora: The best they ever had.
[25] Gyebek: It was not their fault that it was good.
[26] Yuri Dora: No. That’s why the youngest walked into the sea.
[27] ¶ The youngest walked into the sea and would not turn round, and stands there yet as a single rock off the shore. The other four hundred and ninety-nine went up the mountain and wept until they were stone. You can go and count them. Nobody has ever got the same number twice.
[28] Gyebek: I will count them.
[29] Yuri Dora: Everybody says that.
[30] ¶ He counts them on his first free morning and gets four hundred and ninety-eight. He goes back the next morning to find the one he missed.
[31] ❝QUOTE (Chogamje (초감제), Nalgwa-guk-seomgim, recited by Gang Sun-seon (강순선), recorded by Heo Nam-chun, Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2009 — Tapdong Yeongdeung-gut, Jeju City (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)): Five hundred shrines before that mountain, five hundred temples before this one. Five hundred generals, five hundred teachers. One valley short, so it is an island that could raise no king, no tiger, no bear.❞
[32] Yuri Dora: So the island had stone sons, and no bridge. She meant to fix that.
[33] ¶ She asked the islanders for one thing: clothes her size, a hundred rolls of silk, and she would lay a bridge to the mainland. They found ninety-nine. The collar was never finished. Neither was the bridge.
[34] Gyebek: They were one roll short.
[35] Yuri Dora: They were.
[36] Gyebek: …That is the worst amount to be short by.
[37] ¶ He finishes the roof by feel after dark. He comes down with one peg left over, and goes back up to find the hole it belongs in.
[38] ¶ In the morning he cuts a notch in the beam by the door. Nine hundred and sixty.
[39] ¶ **Three princes climb out of the ground. “Not from an egg,” the island insists. Then a box drifts in from the sea…!**
